hypothesis: Batched GPU prefill for expert-pruned checkpoints (pr1 tip) speeds up REAP-132 prefill over upstream dev, which refuses the GPU batch path for a 132-expert model (moe-batch=off) and runs the CPU expert union
model: DeepSeek V4 Flash REAP 150B (puwaer/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-reap-150b, 132 routed experts, fp4 experts / fp8 dense), colibri safetensors layout, 79 GiB on disk
command: build: cd c && make -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr NVCC=/usr/bin/nvcc CUDA_ARCH=sm_86 NO_TC=1 -j8; run: python3 c/coli serve --model <REAP dir> --ram 40 --ctx 8192 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8090, server environment exactly PATH/HOME/USER/LOGNAME/LANG + the config's env keys (env -i); one freshly started server process per sample (OS page cache not dropped between samples, see notes.cache_state), 3 samples per arm interleaved with the arm order rotated per round (A B C E F / B C E F A / C E F A B); client bench_pr1.py sends request 1 (long_prefill: 1992-token prompt, max_tokens 100) and, for arms A/B/C, then request 2 (long_prefill_2: 3005-token prompt, max_tokens 60), streamed, greedy; tok_s = prompt_tokens / time-to-first-token of the named request; metric: request 'long_prefill' (1992 prompt tokens); baseline arm A, trial arm B

hardware.cpu: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 16 cores / 32 threads, 1 socket, governor powersave (amd-pstate), max 5.76 GHz (engine: 16 OpenMP compute threads + 3 expert-loader lanes)
hardware.ram: 62 GiB DDR5 (8 GiB swap); engine --ram 40 (31.6 GiB routed-expert RAM cache, 6.2 GiB dense resident); MemAvailable 46.8 GiB (47933 MiB) at preflight with llama.cpp still loaded
hardware.storage: WD_BLACK SN850X 4 TB NVMe (PCIe 4.0), ext4 root filesystem (rw,relatime), model read with O_DIRECT (v4_ssd_io mode=direct-aligned); OS page cache not dropped between samples; round 1 (samples 1-5) partly cold (serve-unit memory peak 7.9G-14.6G vs 7.3G in all 11 later samples), warm from round 2 on
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic, gcc 13.3.0, Python 3.12.3, CUDA toolkit 12.0.140 (generic build CUDA_ARCH=sm_86 NO_TC=1), NVIDIA driver 595.84; 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24 GB, PCIe 4.0 x16-capable cards running at link width x8, NVLink NV4 bridge; only GPU0 used (COLI_GPU=0 DSV4_CUDA_DEVICE=0)

notes.warmup: warmup_runs 0: request 1 (long_prefill) is the first request the client sends to each freshly started server process; no warm-up request precedes it
notes.cache_state: The OS page cache was not dropped between samples. Round 1 (samples 1-5: A/s1 B/s1 C/s1 E/s1 F/s1) was partly cold: the serve unit's systemd memory peak (its cgroup, which counts the page cache the unit faulted in) was 13.9G A/s1, 14.6G B/s1, 10.2G C/s1, 9.1G E/s1, 7.9G F/s1, against 7.3G in all 11 later samples (evidence/pr1-host-journal.txt); from round 2 on the page cache was warm. Round 1 holds the lowest request-1 decode rate of every arm and the slowest A request-1 TTFT (A s1 223.9 s vs 218.4/219.1 s). Medians are over all 3 samples; the round-1-excluded ratios (s2/s3 means) are in notes.round1_excluded.
notes.round1_excluded: s2/s3 mean tok/s (round 1 excluded): A 9.1069, B 24.2416, ratio 2.6619
notes.variability: TTFT stdev / CV over 3 samples: A r1 3.002 s / 1.36%; B r1 0.131 s / 0.16%; TTFT coefficient of variation (stdev/mean, 3 samples) is <= 0.32% for every arm and request except A request 1 (1.36%, from the partly cold A s1); TTFT stdev is <= 0.268 s except A request 1 (3.002 s) and A request 2 (0.727 s).
notes.earlier_run_2026_10_14: A median 9.0978 tok/s on 2026-10-14 (7b55a9b3) -> 9.0921 here (-0.06%); B median 24.3174 tok/s on 2026-10-14 (48767c01) -> 24.2675 here (-0.21%); all A/B/C/E/F arm/request medians of this run are -0.41% to -0.06% vs 2026-10-14, all lower; the 1-sample verify arm V, request 1: 12.9944 -> 12.9969 (+0.02%); B..F and V ran an earlier pr1 commit then
notes.outputs: 25 outputs in 16 samples (A 6, B 6, C 6, E 3, F 3, V 1), all byte-identical (full-text sha256) to arm A's per-request reference; 19 of them come from the pr1-tip arms B C E F V.
notes.host: Host side effect of the window (llama.cpp down 14:12:54-15:20:51 PDT; evidence/pr1-host-journal.txt): the Hermes shadowfax-ensure-active-stack watchdog ran every 5 min (start to start 300-301 s; 14 runs, 14:13:43-15:20:18), reported the backend unhealthy each time (all 14 exited 1; 12 logged 'backend unhealthy' with restarted_units [] and recovered false, 2 logged no output) and restarted nothing; the first run after the restore (15:23:48) passed. Hermes cron ran without an LLM backend: shadowfax-autonomous-heartbeat (*/30 * * * *) 14:30:23-14:35:37, failed ('RuntimeError: Connection error.'), 4.446s CPU, during samples C/s1 E/s1 F/s1 B/s2; shadowfax-autonomous-heartbeat (*/30 * * * *) 15:00:23-15:05:25, failed ('RuntimeError: Connection error.'), 3.817s CPU, during samples E/s3 F/s3 A/s3.
notes.observation_decode: Observation (not this manifest's hypothesis; already documented in the PR docs, docs/deepseek-v4.md 'Expert-pruned checkpoints (REAP)', review finding F42): decode right after the GPU-batch prefill is slower on the pr1 tip than after dev's CPU-union prefill. Request 1: B 2.0543 vs A 2.2465 chunks/s (s2/s3 means, -8.6%; all 3 samples -7.4%); request 2: B 2.757 vs A 2.825 (-2.4%; all 3 samples -2.4%). Seen in both runs: on 2026-10-14 (pr1 48767c01) -8.0% and -3.1% (s2/s3 means). Decode rate = bench_pr1.py decode_tok_s, streamed chunks per second after the first chunk (25 chunks on request 1, 60 on request 2); the texts are byte-identical, so this is a speed difference only; the cause is not established.
